title: Bug turns one of the biggest fears about Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses into reality
key_facts: Some Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses recorded people's conversations without the wearer saying the 'Hey, Meta' prompt, in a bug Meta says is fixed.

A Reddit user said it happened across three pairs with the 'Respond without Hey Meta' setting off, and that the Meta AI app saved audio and transcripts of the conversations; they first noticed it after a recent firmware update.
Android Authority reported the discussions on Tuesday 13 Oct and published Meta's response that the issue 'has been resolved'.
Meta has not said what caused the bug, whether a firmware update was responsible or how many devices were affected; Android Authority could not replicate the problem.
Ars Technica argues the bug shows the glasses' recording light is not enough to prevent inadvertent recording, and that even a handful of affected devices is a concern.

Earlier this year Swedish journalists reported that contractors at Sama, a data-annotation firm in Kenya, had viewed private footage from the glasses; that led to a lawsuit seeking class-action status and an investigation by Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.
In August Meta updated the glasses so they will not record if the indicator light is covered; Norway is considering a temporary ban on such glasses.
quote_evidence: Some Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses were recording people’s conversations without the wearer knowing.
Meta hasn’t said what caused the Ray-Ban Metas to record people without user consent.
We also don’t know how many Meta smart glasses were affected.
why_it_matters_hint: Wearers and bystanders could be recorded without knowing, though the cause and scale are unknown and Meta says it is fixed.
notes: Read in full at Ars Technica. First reports and Meta's response were on 13 Oct 2026, before the window; not carried in earlier editions.
